Fun fact: naming things on a mission is harder than it sounds. You’d think engineers would just call the camera “camera” and move on, but no. Every instrument, every piece of software, and every weird little subsystem ends up with a nickname, and sometimes the nickname sticks better than the official name. Our spectrometer, for example, is formally something like the Compact Infrared Mapping Spectrometer, but in meetings everyone just calls it “Spec.” The data pipeline is “the Mill” because it grinds through raw files and spits out clean ones. Some names come from acronyms that someone worked backward to make cute. Others come from inside jokes that nobody remembers the origin of. It’s silly, but it makes the work feel more human, and honestly, when you’re debugging at two in the morning, a good nickname helps.
